newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Jet soars on prompt squeeze.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Jet soars on prompt squeeze.

text.p: Singapore front month jet fuel swaps soared at midday Thursday Wednesday on a squeeze on the prompt market as some players looked to cover short sales both on the physical and paper markets, traders said.
"There are very little prompt cargoes around. When we tried to buy some we found that there were few sellers," one trader said.
The February jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade bids rose to $3.60 per barrel from Wednesday's $3.30 buying number, brokers said.
Brokers said there were few deals as most sellers have backed away in the face of escalating physical prices where the spread between jet fuel and gas oil is at a hefty $5.00 per barrel.

In the physical market on Wednesday, 150,000 barrels of gas oil traded at $25.20 per barrel while 100,000 barrels of jet fuel traded at $30.40 per barrel, both on a free-on-board (fob) Singapore basis.
March regrade swaps were largely unchanged with buyers quoted at around $2.00 per barrel again with no firm sellers seen against it.
Gas oil swaps rose in quiet trading on stronger overnight crude values where February Brent crude closed up 52 cents to $22.77 per barrel on London's International Petroleum Exchange.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted at $25.80/$26.00 per barrel from Wednesday's $25.55/$25.75.
Front month Singapore fuel oil swaps edged up slightly to $99.50/$100.50 per tonne, from Wednesday's $99.00/$99.50, brokers said.
Naphtha rose sharply in line with the 52-cent hike to crude values with February buyers quoted at $23.90 per barrel from Wednesday's $23.40/$23.70 per barrel, one broker said.
Brokers said most sellers were sidelined in view of the big rise to crude prices.
